ruleset.name: jpinpoint-kotlin-rules
ruleset.description: jPinpoint rules for responsible Kotlin coding, sponsored by Rabobank. Uses PMD-7.

rule.name: AvoidDecimalAndChoiceFormatAsField
rule.message: Avoid using NumberFormat, DecimalFormat or ChoiceFormat as field since it is thread-unsafe.
rule.description: Problem: java.text.DecimalFormat and java.text.ChoiceFormat are thread-unsafe. Solution: usual solution is to create a new local one when needed in a method. (jpinpoint-rules) (jpinpoint-rules)

property.name: xpath

rule.name: AvoidImplicitlyRecompilingRegex
rule.message: String regex method, Pattern.matches or FileSystem.getPathMatcher is used. Implicitly compiles a regex pattern, can be expensive.
rule.description: A regular expression is compiled implicitly on every invocation. Problem: this can be expensive, depending on the length of the regular expression. Solution: Compile the regex pattern only once and assign it to a private static final Pattern field. java.util.Pattern objects are thread-safe so they can be shared among threads. (jpinpoint-rules)

property.name: xpath

rule.name: AvoidInMemoryStreamingDefaultConstructor
rule.message: The default capacity or smaller is used for ByteArrayOutputStream or StringWriter, it usually needs expensive expansions.
rule.description: The default constructor of ByteArrayOutputStream creates a 32-byte initial capacity and for StringWriter 16 chars. Problem: Such a small buffer as capacity usually needs several expensive expansions. Solution: Pre-size the ByteArrayOutputStream or StringWriter with an initial capacity such that an expansion is not needed in most cases, typically much larger than 32, for instance, 4096. (jpinpoint-rules) (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: AvoidMultipleConcatStatements
rule.message: Multiple statements concatenate to the same String. Use StringBuilder append.
rule.description: Multiple statements concatenate to the same String. Problem: Each statement with one or more +-operators creates a hidden temporary StringBuilder, a char[] and a new String object, which all have to be garbage collected. Solution: Use StringBuilder.append. (jpinpoint-rules)

property.name: xpath

rule.name: AvoidRecompilingPatterns
rule.message: Pattern.compile is used in a method. Compiling a regex pattern can be expensive, make it a constant or instance field.
rule.description: A regular expression is compiled on every invocation. Problem: this can be expensive, depending on the length of the regular expression. Solution: Usually a pattern is a literal, not dynamic and can be compiled only once. Assign it to a private constant or instance field. java.util.Pattern objects are thread-safe so they can be shared among threads. (jpinpoint-rules)

property.name: xpath

rule.name: AvoidRecompilingXPathExpression
rule.message: XPathExpression is created and compiled every time. Beware it is thread-unsafe.
rule.description: XPathExpression is created and compiled on every method call, compiled possibly implicitly by XPath::evaluate. Problem: Creation of XPath and compilation of XPathExpression takes time. It may slow down your application. Solution: 1. Avoid XPath usage. 2. Compile the xpath expression as String into a XPathExpression. However, since XPath and XPathExpression classes are thread-unsafe, they are not easily cached. Caching it in a ThreadLocal may be a solution. (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: AvoidRecreatingDateTimeFormatter
rule.message: Avoid recreating DateTimeFormatter, it is relatively expensive.
rule.description: Problem: Recreating a DateTimeFormatter is relatively expensive. Solution: org.joda.time.format.DateTimeFormatter or Java 8 java.time.DateTimeFormatter is thread-safe and can be shared among threads. Create the formatter from a pattern only once, to initialize a constant or instance field. (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: AvoidSimpleDateFormat
rule.message: SimpleDateFormat is used. Since it is thread-unsafe, it needs expensive recreation.
rule.description: Problem: java.util.SimpleDateFormat is thread-unsafe. The usual solution is to create a new one when needed in a method. Creating SimpleDateFormat is relatively expensive. Solution: Use java.time.DateTimeFormatter. These classes are immutable, thus thread-safe and can be made static. (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: AvoidStringBuffer
rule.message: StringBuffer is used. It introduces locking overhead, use StringBuilder.
rule.description: Problem: StringBuffer introduces locking overhead because it is thread safe. Its thread-safety is rarely needed. Solution: Replace StringBuffer by StringBuilder. (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: AvoidWideScopeXPathExpression
rule.message: XPathExpression targets a wide scope, this is potentially slow.
rule.description: The XPathExpression targets a wide scope since it starts with `//`. Problem: XPath has to search in a wide scope for occurrences, this may take a while. Solution: 1. Avoid XPath usage. 2. Make the scope as narrow as possible, do not start with `//`. (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: AvoidXPathAPIUsage
rule.message: XPathAPI is used. XPathAPI implementation has bad performance.
rule.description: XPathAPI is used. Problem: XPathAPI implementation is slow. Solution: 1. try to avoid using XPathAPI. 2. improve performance by using jvm parameters and possibly CachedXPathAPI. (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: MDCPutWithoutRemove
rule.message: MDC put is used without remove or clear in the same function
rule.description: MDC values are added for logging, but no corresponding remove or clear is performed. Problem: MDC values can leak to other user transactions (requests) and log incorrect information. Solution: remove the MDC value in a finally clause or clear the MDC. (jpinpoint-rules - Kotlin) (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: UnresolvedType
rule.message: A type cannot be resolved. Make sure all dependencies are available on the classpath.
rule.description: Problem: When analyzing Kotlin code, a type reference could not be resolved. This typically means a dependency is missing from the analysis classpath. Several rules (using typeIs, matchesSig) depend on type information; without it they may produce false positives or miss violations. Solution: Make sure all dependencies are available on the auxiliary classpath (--aux-classpath). Compile all source code before running PMD. Note: this rule requires kotlin-type-mapper for type resolution. (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: AvoidCommonPoolForFutureAsync
rule.message: Avoid using the common thread pool for future.supplyAsync, use a separate pool.
rule.description: Problem: CompletableFuture.supplyAsync is typically used for remote calls. By default, it uses the common pool. The number of threads in the common pool is equal to the number of CPUs, which is suitable for in-memory processing. For I/O, however, this number is typically not suitable because most time is spent waiting for the response and not in CPU. The common pool must not be used for blocking calls. Solution: A separate, properly sized, pool of threads (an Executor) should be used for the async calls. (jpinpoint-rules) (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: AvoidCompletionServiceTake
rule.message: Avoid completionService.take, use poll
rule.description: Problem: take() stalls indefinitely in case of hanging threads and consumes a thread. Solution: use poll() with a timeout value and handle the timeout. (jpinpoint-rules) (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: AvoidFutureGetWithoutTimeout
rule.message: Avoid future.get without timeout
rule.description: Problem: Stalls indefinitely in case of hanging threads and consumes a thread. Solution: Provide a timeout value and handle the timeout. (jpinpoint-rules) (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: AvoidFutureJoinWithoutTimeout
rule.message: Avoid future.join without timeout
rule.description: Problem: Stalls indefinitely in case of hanging thread(s) and consumes a thread. Solution: Provide a timeout before the join and handle the timeout. For example a future.get(timeout, unit), an orTimeout() or a completeOnTimeout(). You may want to use CompletableFuture.allOf() too. (jpinpoint-rules) (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: AvoidNonPrivateFieldsInSharedObjects
rule.message: Avoid non-private properties in shared objects. Make properties private to ensure thread-safety.
rule.description: Problem: A singleton, or more general: an object shared among threads, has a property that is not private. These properties can possibly be modified from other classes. Solution: Make the properties private. Note: properties are excluded when annotated with: @Autowired/@Value/@Inject. (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: AvoidUnguardedAssignmentToNonFinalFieldsInObjectsUsingSynchronized
rule.message: Avoid unguarded assignments to non-final fields in objects using synchronized. Access thread-safely AND use @GuardedBy.
rule.description: Problem: Multiple threads typically access fields of an object using synchronized. Unguarded assignment to a non-final (var) field is thread-unsafe and may cause corruption or visibility problems. To make this thread-safe, that is, guard the field e.g. with @Synchronized methods, may cause contention. Solution: Make the properties val and unmodifiable. If they really need to be mutable, make access thread-safe: use @Synchronized and @GuardedBy or @Volatile. Notes: 1. In case you are sure the class is used in a single threaded context only, remove the current use of synchronized and annotate the class with @NotThreadSafe to make this explicit. 2. Use @VisibleForTesting for methods (e.g. setters) used for JUnit only. (jpinpoint-rules) (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: AvoidUnguardedAssignmentToNonFinalFieldsInSharedObjects
rule.message: Avoid unguarded assignments to non-final fields in objects shared among threads. Access thread-safely AND use @GuardedBy.
rule.description: Problem: Multiple threads typically access fields of a singleton or may access fields in session scoped objects. Unguarded assignment to a non-final (var) field is thread-unsafe and may cause corruption or visibility problems. It may also unintentionally mix-up session data. Solution: Make the properties val and unmodifiable. If they really need to be mutable, make access thread-safe: use @Synchronized and @GuardedBy or @Volatile. Notes 1. For autowiring/injection, the assignment of the reference is thread safe, so var is acceptable. The unmodifiable/thread-safe requirement for that field still holds. Also make sure no other thread-unsafe assignment is made to that field. 2. In case you are sure the Component is used in single threaded context only (e.g. a Tasklet), annotate the class with @NotThreadSafe to make this explicit. (jpinpoint-rules) (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: AvoidUnguardedMutableFieldsInObjectsUsingSynchronized
rule.message: Avoid unguarded non-final or mutable fields in objects using synchronized. Make final immutable or access thread-safely AND use @GuardedBy.
rule.description: Problem: Multiple threads typically access fields of an object using synchronized. If a field or its reference is mutable, access is thread-unsafe and may cause corruption or visibility problems. To make this thread-safe, that is, guard the field e.g. with synchronized methods, may cause contention. Solution: Make the properties val and unmodifiable. If they really need to be mutable, make access thread-safe: use @Synchronized and @GuardedBy or @Volatile. Notes: 1. Instances of Date, StringBuilder, URL and File are examples of mutable objects and should be avoided (or else guarded) as fields of shared objects. 2. Instances of classes like ArrayList, HashMap and HashSet are also mutable and should be properly wrapped or use thread-safe implementations like ConcurrentHashMap. 3. For autowiring/injection, the assignment of the reference is thread safe, so var is acceptable. The unmodifiable/thread-safe requirement still holds. 4. In case you are sure the class is used in single threaded context only, remove the current use of synchronized and annotate the class with @NotThreadSafe to make this explicit. (jpinpoint-rules) (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: AvoidUnguardedMutableInheritedFieldsInSharedObjects
rule.message: Mutator method called on inherited field. Avoid unguarded mutable inherited fields in objects shared among threads. Make final immutable or access thread-safely AND use @GuardedBy.
rule.description: Problem: Multiple threads typically access fields of a singleton or may access fields in session scoped objects. If a (inherited) field or its reference is mutable, access is thread-unsafe and may cause corruption or visibility problems. It may also unintentionally mix-up session data. Solution: Make the fields val and unmodifiable. If they really need to be mutable, make access thread-safe: use @Synchronized and @GuardedBy or @Volatile. Notes: 1. Instances of Date, StringBuilder, URL and File are examples of mutable objects and should be avoided (or else guarded) as fields of shared objects. 2. Instances of classes like ArrayList, HashMap and HashSet are also mutable and should be properly wrapped or use thread-safe implementations like ConcurrentHashMap. 3. For autowiring/injection, the assignment of the reference is thread safe, so var is acceptable. 4. In case you are sure the Component is used in single threaded context only, annotate the class with @NotThreadSafe to make this explicit. (jpinpoint-rules) (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: NotProperlySynchronizingOnFieldWhileUsingGuardedBy
rule.message: Not properly synchronizing access of field while using @GuardedBy(field)
rule.description: Problem: The field to which the `@GuardedBy` annotation is applied is not accessed thread-safely as promised by GuardedBy. Solution: Make access thread-safe: synchronize access by a `synchronized(lock)` block with `lock` being a private val field. Note that methods with annotations `@Autowired`, `@PostConstruct`, `@BeforeStep`, `@Value` and `@Inject` are ignored. (jpinpoint-rules) (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: NotProperlySynchronizingOnThisWhileUsingGuardedBy
rule.message: Not properly synchronizing access of field while using @GuardedBy('this')
rule.description: Problem: The field to which this annotation is applied should only be accessed when holding the built-in 'this' lock by using synchronized. Solution: Make access thread-safe: synchronize access by @Synchronized method annotation or a synchronized(this) block. Note that methods with annotations @Autowired, @PostConstruct, @BeforeStep, @Value and @Inject are ignored. (jpinpoint-rules) (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: WrongUseOfGuardedBy
rule.message: @GuardedBy or locking is used in a wrong way, this may indicate a concurrency bug.
rule.description: Problem: Wrong use of locking and '@GuardedBy' may result in thread-unsafety and concurrency bugs. It may obstruct other GuardedBy rules which check whether the promise of guarding is actually met, it may disguise high-risk violations. Solution: Use '@GuardedBy' properly: use a private val lock object; a String literal of the lock name as '@GuardedBy' argument; and use that explicit or 'this' lock with 'synchronized'. (jpinpoint-rules) (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: HttpClientBuilderWithoutDisableConnectionState
rule.message: A HttpClient builder is used and disableConnectionState is not called. HTTP client tracks connection state while using TLS.
rule.description: Problem: NTLM authenticated connections and SSL/TLS connections with client certificate authentication are stateful: they have a specific user identity/security context per session. If HttpClients have enabled connection state tracking which is the default, established TLS connections will not be reused because it is assumed that the user identity or security context may differ. Then performance will suffer due to a full TLS handshake for each request. Solution: HttpClients should disable connection state tracking in order to reuse TLS connections, since service calls for one pool have the same user identity/security context for all sessions. (jpinpoint-rules) (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: HttpClientBuilderWithoutPoolSize
rule.message: HttpClient builder connection pool is not configured.
rule.description: Problem: when the [default max connections per route] external calls are being made to the same host, the next thread requesting a connection to that host must wait for a free connection. For Apache HttpClient v4, this default = 2 and for v5 this default = 5, often too low. Max total connections are 20 and 25 respectively. Solution: HttpClients should explicitly define the number of connections per route. If only one route is used, make the max number of connections equal to conn per route. Solution: 1. use setConnectionManager and call setMaxTotal and setDefaultMaxPerRoute on that connection manager, or 2. use no ConnectionManager, call setMaxConnTotal and setMaxConnPerRoute on the client directly (v4 only). (jpinpoint-rules) (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: NettyConnectionProviderWithoutMaxOrTimeout
rule.message: Netty ConnectionProvider has no defined maxConnections or pendingAcquireTimeout.
rule.description: Problem: If a Reactor Netty Connection Provider is built without an explicit `maxConnections`, this defaults to `max(#CPU, 8) * 2`. This is often too low, leading to throttling, delays and too long response times. If the provider is built without an explicit `pendingAcquireTimeout`, this defaults to `45s`. This is often too high, leading to unnecessary long waiting times. Solution: Define both `maxConnections` and `pendingAcquireTimeout` with proper values, for instance, `50` and `300 [ms]` respectively. (jpinpoint-rules) (jpinpoint-rules)
